newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi arrests 19,000 beggars over one year.
newsitem.headline: Saudi arrests 19,000 beggars over one year.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has arrested some 19,700 beggars across the kingdom in one year of its anti-begging campaign, the daily Arab News said on Sunday.

"A source at the ministry of labour and social affairs explained that of the total figure, 9,000 were men while 10,700 were women, 15,000 were non-Saudis while 4,700 were Saudis," the English-language newspaper said. It did not give dates for the one-year period.

It said the "anti-begging department" in the Islamic holy city of Mecca had arrested 8,700 beggars in the year, making it the most active of the 12 regional departments participating in the crackdown.
The ministry source said most of the beggars were below the age of 18, and more than 8,500 had some sort of handicap. About 5,000 of the beggars were classified as children.
Diplomats in the kingdom say the number of beggars in Saudi Arabia is on the rise. While there are no official unemployment figures, analysts say the jobless rate is above 10 percent and rising.
Saudi Arabia earlier this year expelled over 150 Indian child beggars in its bid to clamp down on begging.

Thousands of foreign nationals, many of them from the Indian subcontinent, come to oil-rich Saudi Arabia in hopes of earning more than they could at home. Many come as guest workers or haj pilgrims but stay beyond the period permitted by their visas.
